oi.text: We believe that providing historical and adjusted net income and adjusted net income per diluted share, exclusive of such items as reversals of tax reserves, net discrete tax expenses (benefits), restructuring charges and reversals, intangible amortization, stock-based compensation, other non-operating income/expense, gains on asset sales and acquisition-related expenses, permits investors to compare results with prior periods that did not include these items. Management uses the aforementioned non-GAAP measures to monitor and evaluate ongoing operating results and trends and to gain an understanding of our comparative operating performance. In addition, certain of our stockholders have expressed an interest in seeing financial performance measures exclusive of the impact of these matters, which while important, are not central to the core operations of our business.

da_op.text: This release includes adjusted net income, adjusted net income per diluted share and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA"), each of which is a non-GAAP financial measure.

nonop.text: During the first fiscal quarter of 2026, Digi modified its method of calculating adjusted net income and adjusted net income per diluted share to include the impact of interest expense. This change was primarily driven by the continued use of financing by the Company to fund cash flow needs and therefore including the recurring nature of interest presents a better metric that management believes provides a more representative view of operating performance and cash-generating capability. Accordingly, we evaluated the impact of this change on prior-period disclosures and have recast adjusted net income and adjusted net income per diluted share for all periods to conform to this presentation.

tax.text: (1) The tax effect from the above adjustments assumes an estimated effective tax rate of 18.0% for fiscal 2026 and 2025 based on adjusted net income.

net.text: Reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to their closest GAAP analogs appear at the end of this release, as well as a discussion of recent changes to the method of calculating adjusted net income and adjusted net income per diluted share.

da.text: This release includes adjusted net income, adjusted net income per diluted share and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA"), each of which is a non-GAAP financial measure.

sbc.text: We believe that providing historical and adjusted net income and adjusted net income per diluted share, exclusive of such items as reversals of tax reserves, net discrete tax expenses (benefits), restructuring charges and reversals, intangible amortization, stock-based compensation, other non-operating income/expense, gains on asset sales and acquisition-related expenses, permits investors to compare results with prior periods that did not include these items. Management uses the aforementioned non-GAAP measures to monitor and evaluate ongoing operating results and trends and to gain an understanding of our comparative operating performance. In addition, certain of our stockholders have expressed an interest in seeing financial performance measures exclusive of the impact of these matters, which while important, are not central to the core operations of our business.

net sales.text: For the first fiscal quarter, revenues are estimated to be $140 million to $144 million. Adjusted EBITDA is estimated to be between $39.5 million and $41.0 million. Adjusted net income per diluted share is anticipated to be between $0.71 and $0.75 per diluted share, assuming a weighted average diluted share count of 39.5 million. This includes an expected impact from interest of $0.02 to $0.04 per diluted share.

intro.text: Digi International Inc. ("Digi ® ," "we," "our," or "us") was incorporated in 1985 as a Minnesota corporation. We reorganized as a Delaware corporation in 1989 in conjunction with our initial public offering. Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market tier of the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (the "Nasdaq") under the symbol DGII. Our World Headquarters is located at 9350 Excelsior Blvd., Suite 700, Hopkins, Minnesota 55343. The telephone number at our World Headquarters is (952) 912-3444. We are a leading global provider of business and mission-critical Internet of Things ("IoT") connectivity products, services and solutions. We help our customers deploy, monitor and manage critical communications infrastructures that deliver important information in demanding environments with high levels of security and reliability.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: The segment represents approximately 25% of total revenues.
These third parties accounted for 60.2%, 56.7% and 59.9% of our total consolidated revenue in fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
We had one distributor customer of Digi's IoT Products & Services segment that represented 13 % of consolidated revenue for the twelve months ended September 30, 2025.
Our U.S. export sales represented 20.5 %, 28.7 % and 27.2 % of revenue for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
We rely on third party foundries or companies who rely on third party foundries for our semiconductor devices that are Application Specific Integrated Circuits ("ASICs").

We depend on manufacturing relationships and a broad set of suppliers, some of whom provide us with limited-source components and parts, and disruptions in these relationships may cause damage to our customer relationships or otherwise negatively impact our business.

Although most of the components of our products are available from multiple vendors, we have several single-source supplier relationships, either because alternative sources are not available or because the relationship is advantageous to us.
Whether we are successful in this business model depends on a number of factors, including:

Although Ventus has a longer operating history and some of the marketplaces in which it operates are quite mature, new use cases continue to emerge as businesses increasingly rely on self-service devices in their operations with customers.
We also rely on cloud-based technologies for our solutions, as well as our internal systems.
Further, many of our business applications that we rely upon to operate our business now exist within cloud platforms that are managed by third parties.

Our revenue could decline if we are unable to deliver continued access to digital cellular wireless carriers that we depend on to provide sufficient network capacity, reliability and security to our customers.

Certain products rely on the current configuration of radio bands by FCC or other governmental regulatory bodies could require the redesign of existing and future products, which could have an adverse impact on our business.
There can be no assurance that we will recover our investments in SmartSense by Digi / Jolt or Ventus or that we will realize ongoing and consistent profits from these businesses.
